## Project Guidelines

These guidelines supplement the default review criteria and may add repo-specific expectations or constraints.

This repo (ddflow) is a work-queue kernel and MCP server for AI coding agents. It is event-sourced: an append-only JSONL log is the sole source of truth and everything else is a deterministic projection. Always state whether a finding is CONFIRMED (you traced or reproduced it) or THEORETICAL.

Prioritise the bug classes this project has actually shipped and then found, in rough order of how often they were real:

1. Vacuous pass — a check that cannot fail. A gate satisfied by an assertion with no evidence; `all()` over an empty collection; a test that passes with the feature disabled; a tool that exits 0 while reporting it could not run. This is the defining class here: "unavailable" must NEVER render as "success", and "nobody looked" must never render as "no".
2. Three-valued collapse — a tri-state (yes / no / could-not-tell) flattened into a boolean. Timeouts and spawn failures reported as absence; a probe that never ran cached as a negative result.
3. Silent-knob-drop — a config field accepted and never read, or dropped one layer down. Also a knob whose value is validated but discarded.
4. Duplicate-then-drift — the same quantity or logic defined twice, one shadowing the other. A dead fallback branch nothing executes, which therefore cannot be caught drifting. A top-level name defined twice in one module.
5. Metadata-key-vs-field — provenance carried as prose in a free-text body instead of a structured field, forcing a regex to recover it.
6. Projection drops a field — an event handler that silently discards keys the writer recorded, so the fold loses data the log still has.
7. Unreachable state used as a criterion — judging something by a status it can never attain (e.g. asking whether a command-line tool is "registered" as an MCP server).
8. Exit-code semantics — this project's vocabulary is 0 healthy, 1 failure, 2 could-not-run/nothing, 3 coordination refused. Collapsing 2 into 0 is a bug, always.
9. Concurrency — `fcntl.flock` is per open-file-description, so a second lock on one file in one process deadlocks against itself. Check-then-act outside a transaction. A lock held across an O(all-events) read. Process-global state (`sys.stdout`) swapped per call in something that may become reentrant.
10. Identity and attribution — anything that assumes one agent per process, per tree, or per connection. Several agents sharing a derived identity is a correctness bug, not a cosmetic one: reviewer independence is a comparison of agent against author.
11. Torn-tail resume — half-written state on restart; a non-atomic write with a fixed temp filename.
12. CLI/MCP divergence — the two surfaces are meant to be parity-tested. A capability on one and not the other, or the same operation encoded differently on each.

Also flag, specifically: a docstring that promises behaviour the code does not implement (this project has shipped that twice), and any source change that arrives without a runnable regression test demonstrating the defect.
